page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a burstable CPU allocation model. It features 480 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix multiplication. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe storage and relies on external network storage, supported by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded capabilities and substantial memory throughput. Single-core evaluation via Geekbench records a score of 2137.0, supported by solid single-threaded data compression throughput in gzip (34.06 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.32 GB/sec). Geekbench text processing achieved a top-tier score of 2929.0. In multi-threaded evaluations, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance reached 8656.33 and Geekbench multi-core reached 8350.0, placing them within median performance bands. Memory benchmarks showed read-only cached bandwidth of 643.08 GB/sec and uncached block throughput of 76.14 GB/sec read and 48.41 GB/sec write. In-memory data store operations on Redis reached 15.37 million SET operations per second, while LLM text generation on a 7B model ran at 8.5 tokens per second.

As part of the Flex tier, the instance balances cost efficiency and compute availability by pairing burstable CPU performance with standard enterprise memory capacity. This design enables a cost profile lower than dedicated baseline compute while retaining full access to DDR5 memory bandwidth. Workload tradeoffs involve the absence of onboard scratch storage and burstable compute limits during continuous multi-core execution. The instance is well matched for mid-sized in-memory databases, Redis caches, data indexing, batch compression pipelines, and text-processing services with intermittent processor demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro system, running an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8 burstable vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 480 MB of L3 cache, it delivers clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz and includes AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server pairs this compute configuration with 64.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB per core. It offers a 2 Gbps baseline network link, lacks local storage, and includes no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread execution, rapid text processing, and solid in-memory cache operations, though sustained multi-core compute remains bounded by the burstable allocation model. The instance is structured for memory-heavy, bursty tasks including Redis caching, in-memory databases, text parsing, and data preprocessing pipelines.
